```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)

# A throwaway pharos project holding the package's SCM fixtures: the planned
# process under extdata/models/scm and a completed one under
# extdata/models/scm-complete. Their records are relative to this root.
vignette_root <- tempfile("hyperion-scm-")
models <- file.path(vignette_root, "extdata", "models")
dir.create(models, recursive = TRUE)
file.copy(
  system.file("extdata", "models", c("scm", "scm-complete"), package = "hyperion"),
  models,
  recursive = TRUE
)
file.copy(system.file("pharos.toml", package = "hyperion"), vignette_root)
options(hyperion.config_dir = vignette_root)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = vignette_root)
```

```{r setup}
library(hyperion)
```

hyperion drives pharos' stepwise covariate modeling (SCM) from R. An SCM
process starts from an **initial model** whose `$THETA` records already declare
every covariate effect to be tested, runs forward selection (each round fits
one model per untested candidate and adds the best significant one) and
backward elimination (each round refits with one retained effect fixed and
drops the least significant), and writes a final model with exactly the
retained effects. Scoring is a likelihood-ratio test on the change in OFV.
Every fit runs on slurm; a one-CPU driver job submits and waits for them.

The pieces mirror the model workflow: `read_scm()` reads the process's config
the way `read_model()` reads a model, `check_scm()` mirrors `check_model()`,
`summary()` works on the object, and `submit_scm_to_slurm()` sits beside
`submit_model_to_slurm()`.

# The initial model

Each candidate effect is a `$THETA`, conventionally `(0 FIX)` so it is switched
off, named by its comment. The name is what the project's comment dialect
(`[nonmem.comments] type` in `pharos.toml`) parses as the theta's name, so
`; WT_CL (cov)` names `WT_CL` under both dialects. Those names are what the
config refers to.

```{r model, results='asis'}
mod <- read_model("extdata/models/scm/1001.mod")
mod
```

# Setting up the process

`init_scm()` writes the config, `<stem>scm.toml`, beside the process's own
directory (`scm/<stem>/` next to the model by default) and returns it as an
object. `effects` names the candidates; an effect that needs more than its
name is given as a row or an `ScmEffect`. Options are edited by assignment on
the object and written back with `write_scm()`.

```{r init}
dir.create("extdata/models/scm-demo")
file.copy(
  c("extdata/models/scm/1001.mod", "extdata/models/scm/data.csv"),
  "extdata/models/scm-demo"
)

scm <- init_scm(
  "extdata/models/scm-demo/1001.mod",
  effects = list(
    "WT_CL",
    list(name = "WT_V", type = "categorical", initial = 1, lower = 0, upper = 5)
  )
)
scm$forward_alpha <- 0.01
scm <- write_scm(scm)
```

```{r print-scm, results='asis'}
scm
```

The written file keeps pharos' explanatory comments for every key the object
did not change. It can be edited by hand too, and `read_scm()` reads it back.

The effects are `ScmEffect` objects, held under `scm$covariates$effects`.
`add_scm_effect()` and `remove_scm_effect()` change them on the object;
`write_scm()` writes the result.

```{r effects}
scm <- read_scm("extdata/models/scm-demo/scm/1001scm.toml")
scm <- add_scm_effect(scm, "CRCL_CL", initial = 0.5)
scm <- remove_scm_effect(scm, "WT_V")
scm$covariates$effects[[2]]
scm <- write_scm(scm)
```

# Checking the plan

`check_scm()` resolves the config to its plan without writing or running
anything: the candidates and the thetas they name, the options, the worst case
number of fits, and pharos' warnings. Once a process has started it also
reports where it stands and whether the config changed since.

```{r check, results='asis'}
check_scm(scm)
```

A name that does not match a `$THETA` comment is the most common problem, and
the error lists the names pharos did resolve.

# Submitting, following and stopping

`submit_scm_to_slurm()` queues the driver job and returns. It needs the
`pharos` CLI on `PATH` at the version hyperion was built for, the slurm tools,
and partitions that exist; it refuses a completed process unless
`overwrite = TRUE`, and a plan the running process cannot resume under.

```{r submit, eval = FALSE}
submit_scm_to_slurm(scm, partition = "cpu")
#> ✔ Submitted the SCM process as slurm job 4242 (scm_1001)
#> ℹ Log: .slurm-logs/scm_1001_4242.out
#> Follow it with `get_scm_status("extdata/models/scm-demo/scm/1001")`; stop it
#> with `stop_scm("extdata/models/scm-demo/scm/1001")`.
```

`get_scm_status()` reads the process off disk at the time of the call: each
decided round with its table, the open round fit by fit, and whether the
driver is still running. `stop_scm()` pauses the process (the driver is
stopped, fits still in the queue are cancelled, running fits finish and are
used on resume); submitting the config again resumes it. `num_rounds` pauses
after that many rounds, and a config change resumes from where the process
stands unless it changes the candidates it was built on.

```{r follow, eval = FALSE}
get_scm_status(scm)
stop_scm(scm)
submit_scm_to_slurm(scm) # resumes
submit_scm_to_slurm(scm, overwrite = TRUE) # starts over
```

# Reading the results

The package ships a completed process as a fixture. `get_scm_status()` and
`summary()` return the process record (what pharos writes to
`scm_summary.json`) and print pharos' own rendering.

```{r status-complete, results='asis'}
done <- read_scm("extdata/models/scm-complete/scm/1001scm.toml")
get_scm_status(done)
```

`summary()` takes the same options as `pharos nonmem scm summary`: `round` and
`candidate` narrow the text, `long`, `timing` and `files` add detail. The
returned object is always the whole record.

```{r summary-round, results='asis'}
summary(done, round = "forward_round1", long = TRUE)
```

`get_scm_candidates()` flattens every round into a data frame, one row per
candidate per round.

```{r candidates}
s <- summary(done)
cand <- get_scm_candidates(s)
cand[, c("round", "candidate", "ofv", "delta_ofv", "p_value", "significant", "selected")]
```

Every model the process wrote is a model like any other. `read_scm_model()`
reads the final, forward, initial or reference model, or one round's
candidate, so `summary()`, `get_parameters()` and the rest work on it.

```{r final}
final <- read_scm_model(s)
summary(final)$run_name
get_parameters(final)
```

# What stays in the CLI

`pharos nonmem scm run`, which drives the process from a terminal instead of a
slurm job, is not wrapped: it blocks until the process ends and takes over the
terminal. Everything else in `pharos nonmem scm` has a hyperion function.

| pharos                    | hyperion                     |
|---------------------------|------------------------------|
| `scm init`                | `init_scm()`                 |
| edit `<stem>scm.toml`     | `read_scm()`, `add_scm_effect()`, `remove_scm_effect()`, `write_scm()` |
| `scm plan`                | `check_scm()`                |
| `scm slurm submit`        | `submit_scm_to_slurm()`      |
| `scm status`              | `get_scm_status()`           |
| `scm stop`                | `stop_scm()`                 |
| `scm summary`             | `summary()`                  |
